title: Expand MCP search filters and pagination for agent workflows
description:
Problem: current MemorySmith search tools expose bounded result counts and core filters (`query`, `tags`, `status`, and tool-specific limits), but they do not expose agent-friendly recency filters, score-threshold controls, or pagination. The Claude benchmark surfaced this gap while trying to build iterative retrieval workflows that need to window large result sets, prefer recently updated records, or discard weak semantic matches without brittle client-side post-processing. Public docs and task search show no current owner for that ergonomics gap.

Evidence from 2026-05-26 audit:
- `README.md` and `Data/Pages/guides/search-and-chat.md` document only the current `query`/`tags`/`status`/`limit`-style arguments.
- `MemorySmith.App/Services/ChatToolCatalog.cs` and the current search controllers expose no `updatedAfter`, `updatedBefore`, `minScore`, or offset/cursor pagination parameters on the MCP search tools.
- The Claude benchmark recommendations call out `minScore`, `updatedAfter`/`updatedBefore`, and pagination as missing but useful for agent workflows.
- Search of `Data/Tasks` found no existing task that owns search-filter or pagination expansion for MCP/agent use.

Desired outcome: external agents can run multi-step retrieval workflows with bounded server-side filtering instead of repeatedly overfetching and trimming results client-side.

Scope:
- In scope: evaluating and, if accepted, adding optional date filters, score-threshold semantics, and pagination/windowing for the MCP search surfaces most useful to agents.
- In scope: defining score semantics carefully so filters are meaningful for lexical, semantic, hybrid, and unified search rather than misleading.
- Out of scope: page embeddings, major ranking redesign, or breaking existing tool signatures.

Acceptance criteria:
- A documented decision exists for whether and where to add recency filters, score-threshold controls, and pagination.
- Any accepted parameters are implemented with backward-compatible defaults and clear semantics.
- Focused tests cover the new filtering/pagination behavior.
- Public docs explain the new parameters and any limitations, especially around score interpretation.

Validation:
- Add focused tests for the affected search tools/endpoints.
- Run the affected MCP/search test slice.
- Run `./Scripts/Test-TaskRecords.ps1` after task creation/update.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body:
## Council Review — Search Ergonomics: Which Filters Actually Help Agents vs. Which Are Traps

**Context:** External agent benchmark across 3 sessions tested all search filter combinations. Live evidence on which are useful, which are missing, and critically: which proposed additions would be misleading given the current scoring architecture.

**Assumptions:**
- `[critical assumption]` `format=json` and `format=envelope` now return identical payloads for MCP tools (confirmed 2026-05-29). The raw lexical and semantic scores are already in the `matchReason` string, not as discrete numeric fields.
- `[assumption]` The `tags` filter in `unified_search` applies to memories only — pages do not share the memory tag schema, so tag filtering is asymmetric in unified search.
- `[assumption]` The `status` filter applies to memory records only. Task status is a separate filter on `task_list`. Page search has no status concept.

---

### The Advocate *(confidence: 88%)*
> **Position:** Three additions have high value and low semantic risk: `updatedAfter` date filter, `excludeIds` list, and `offset` pagination. A fourth — `minScore` — is valuable but needs careful scoping to the semantic component, not the fused RRF score.

**`updatedAfter` / `updatedBefore`:** `lastUpdated` is already returned on every record. Adding it as a filter requires only an index or scan-time predicate. Zero semantic ambiguity — a date is a date. The benchmark confirmed the most recent records are often the most relevant; an `updatedAfter` filter lets agents build "what changed since X" workflows cleanly.

**`excludeIds`:** Iterative research workflows need "more like this, but not this." Currently agents must fetch, extract IDs they've already seen, and hope the next search returns new records. An `excludeIds` list solves this trivially.

**`offset` pagination:** With ~55 records now and growing (TSK-0203 and related feature work are adding more), a 50-record limit with no offset will become a ceiling. Standard `offset` + `limit` is the minimal fix. Cursor pagination is more robust for live data but significantly more complex.

**`minScore` on semantic component:** The benchmark measured garbage queries returning scores of 0.74–0.75 vs. meaningful queries returning 0.82–0.86. An 8% gap is meaningful but only if the threshold is applied to the semantic cosine component, not the fused RRF score (which is 0.009–0.033 and not interpretable as confidence). If `minScore` is applied to the wrong score, it will silently drop relevant records or never filter anything. This needs explicit documentation: "minScore applies to semantic cosine similarity, not hybrid RRF score."

### The Devil's Advocate *(confidence: 72%)*
> **Position:** `minScore` against the semantic component is a footgun unless callers deeply understand the scoring model, and most won't.

The benchmark showed semantic scores compressed into a 0.74–0.87 range for all queries, meaningful or not. A caller setting `minScore=0.80` would drop 40% of relevant results for queries that are syntactically near the record wording (e.g., searching for a specific exact term that has low semantic similarity but high lexical relevance). Hybrid results are ranked by RRF, not by semantic component alone; a high-RRF record could have a semantic score of 0.77 and still be the most relevant result for a lexically dominant query. Exposing `minScore` without surface-level explanation of what it applies to will result in agents filtering out their best results. The safer version is `minScore` only on `memorysmith_semantic_search` (not hybrid), where the score is the sole ranking signal.

### The Pragmatist *(confidence: 85%)*
> **Position:** Ship `updatedAfter`, `excludeIds`, and `offset` as unambiguous low-risk additions. Defer `minScore` until the scoring model is stable and the parameter's semantics can be documented precisely.

These three have no scoring-model dependencies and directly address confirmed agent friction from the benchmark. `updatedAfter` / `updatedBefore` as ISO-8601 strings applied to the `lastUpdated` index field. `excludeIds` as a comma-separated list of memory record IDs to skip in results. `offset` as a non-negative integer default 0. All three are backward-compatible (defaults produce current behavior) and all three have zero semantic ambiguity. For `minScore`: log it as a design note on this task rather than a backlog item until the scoring semantics for hybrid vs. semantic contexts are written down.

### The Historian *(confidence: 75%)*
> **Position:** The tag-filter any-match behavior is already live and working but undocumented. The structured namespace tags (`kind:`, `scope:`, `audience:`) are the highest-leverage existing filter mechanism and should be the first thing documented in the search ergonomics guide.

Live benchmark confirmed: `tags=kind:fact,audience:agent` returns records matching EITHER tag (any-match semantics). `tags` filter applies to memories in unified_search but NOT to pages (pages don't carry the same tag schema). `status` values for memories are `Unconsolidated`, `Working`, `Core`, `Deprecated` — not the task status names. The old skill had wrong status values (`Active`, `Backlog`) that would cause silent misses. Documentation of these filter semantics is the single cheapest ergonomics improvement available — zero code required.

---

### Open Questions
- [ ] Does `tags` filter in `unified_search` apply to page search at all, or is it silently ignored for pages? If silently ignored, this should be documented explicitly to prevent agent confusion.
- [ ] Is there an index on `lastUpdated` for memory records, or would `updatedAfter` require a full scan with a predicate? If full scan, performance characteristics should be documented.
- [ ] For `offset` pagination: does the result set stay stable between paginated calls, or can inserts/updates to the index shift results mid-pagination? If unstable, cursor pagination may be necessary for correctness.

### Confidence Summary
| Dimension | Confidence | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| updatedAfter / excludeIds / offset value | 88% | All confirmed via benchmark as genuine friction points; implementation is straightforward |
| minScore value | 60% | Genuinely useful but scoping to hybrid vs semantic is tricky; risk of footgun is high |
| Documentation-only improvements | 95% | Zero-cost, confirmed-correct via live testing; just needs writing |
| Any-match tag semantics documentation needed | 95% | Confirmed live; `kind:fact,audience:agent` returns either-match; undocumented |
